params.query: MOFCOM GACC announcement 2023 No. 39 graphite export control December 1 2023

items.question: When did China's 2023 graphite export licensing take effect, and under which announcement number?
items.result_summary: IEA, Mayer Brown and Hogan Lovells describe Joint Announcement No. 39 of 2023, issued 20 Oct 2023 and effective 1 Dec 2023. It adds sensitive synthetic and natural flake graphite items to formal export control. Other results covered the Oct 2025 No. 58 battery/anode controls and their suspension under No. 70.
items.interpretation: Claim 1 holds. The announcement date (20 Oct) differs from the effective date (1 Dec).

params.query: active anode material China final determination antidumping countervailing Federal Register February 2026

items.question: What are the Federal Register citations and dates for Commerce's final AD/CVD determinations on Chinese active anode material?
items.result_summary: Federal Register pages list 91 FR 7247 (AD, A-570-194, FR Doc 2026-02998) and 91 FR 7261 (CVD, C-570-195, FR Doc 2026-02999), both published and applicable 17 Feb 2026. trade.gov says Commerce announced the decisions on 11 Feb 2026.
items.interpretation: The citations are correct, but the FR publication date is 17 Feb, not ~11 Feb. The 11 Feb date is the announcement.

params.query: IRS Notice 2026-15 prohibited foreign entity material assistance

items.question: Was IRS Notice 2026-15 issued on 12 Feb 2026 as the first PFE material-assistance guidance?
items.result_summary: The IRS notice PDF, the regulations.gov docket and several law firms confirm that Treasury and the IRS released Notice 2026-15 on 12 Feb 2026. It gives interim MACR guidance and safe harbors under 45X, 45Y and 48E, citing Pub. L. 119-21 of 4 Jul 2025.
items.interpretation: Claim 4 holds, and the primary text also confirms the OBBBA enactment date.

params.query: USITC vote active anode material China injury determination 2026

items.question: What did the USITC decide on active anode material from China, and when?
items.result_summary: A USITC release and the calendar show a notational vote on 12 Mar 2026 with a negative outcome, framed as 'material retardation' of a US industry. USITC Publication 5719 confirms the FR citations and notes that the final scope excludes AAM in lithium-ion battery products.
items.interpretation: Claim 5 holds on the date and outcome. The legal basis was material retardation, not injury.

params.query: final dumping margins China-wide rate countervailing subsidy rates all others

items.question: What exact AD and CVD rates did Commerce set?
items.result_summary: The ITA fact sheet lists a 93.50% dumping margin for separate-rate exporter/producer pairs (BTR, Shanshan and Zhongke Shinzoom entities among them) and 102.72% for the China-wide entity. Subsidy rates are 66.82% (AFA respondents) and 66.86% (Panasonic Global Procurement China and All Others).
items.interpretation: The AD range of 93.5-102.7% is confirmed. The CVD rate should read 66.82-66.86%. BTR and Zhongke Shinzoom were named respondents/producers.

items.question: What is the exact wording and vote of the USITC final determination?
items.result_summary: The Commission found that the subject imports have not materially retarded the establishment of a US industry. Karpel and Johanson voted negative and Kearns affirmative, so Commerce will issue no AD or CVD orders.
items.interpretation: No duty orders exist. The project should describe this as a negative material-retardation finding (2-1).

params.query: Public Law 119-21 One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4 2025 prohibited foreign entity material assistance 45X

items.question: Was the OBBBA signed on 4 Jul 2025, and did it add PFE material-assistance limits to 45X/45Y/48E?
items.result_summary: The IRS newsroom, EY and K&L Gates confirm that P.L. 119-21 was signed 4 Jul 2025 and added PFE restrictions and a material-assistance test (IRC 7701(a)(51)-(52)) to 45X, 45Y and 48E. Entity-level restrictions also reach other credits.
items.interpretation: Claim 2 holds.

params.query: MOFCOM Announcement No. 58 2025 artificial graphite anode export control suspended Announcement 70 November 10 2026

items.question: What did China do on graphite anode export controls in 2025, and are they in force?
items.result_summary: No. 58 of 2025 (9 Oct 2025) would have controlled lithium-battery, cathode and artificial-graphite-anode items from 8 Nov 2025. No. 70 (7 Nov 2025) suspended it with Nos. 55-57, 61 and 62 until 10 Nov 2026. Pillsbury notes that No. 72 separately suspends the stricter US end-use review for dual-use graphite until 27 Nov 2026. One trade site claims an extension to 10 Jan 2027.
items.interpretation: This is an important newer action. The anode-level controls are announced but paused, and the 2023 graphite licensing still applies.

params.query: Treasury IRS prohibited foreign entity guidance proposed regulations specified foreign entity foreign-influenced entity 2026

items.question: Has Treasury issued PFE guidance beyond Notice 2026-15?
items.result_summary: All results were commentary on Notice 2026-15 (Nelson Mullins, K&L Gates, Pillsbury, A&O Shearman, McGuireWoods, IRB 2026-11). They note that proposed regulations and statutory safe-harbor tables are due by 31 Dec 2026, with comments closing 30 Mar 2026.
items.interpretation: No newer PFE guidance surfaced, and the definition of effective control is still open.

params.query: China extends suspension export controls lithium battery graphite anode MOFCOM announcement 2026

items.question: Has China extended the suspension of its Oct 2025 battery and anode export controls beyond 10 Nov 2026?
items.result_summary: Sources from Aug-Oct 2026 still describe the suspension as running to 10 Nov 2026. TIMEWELL says MOFCOM describes the arrangement as running to 10 Jan 2027 but found no formal announcement extending No. 70. CFR notes that the controls would activate in Nov 2026 without an extension.
items.interpretation: The extension is unverified. The project should flag 10 Nov 2026 as a live deadline.

params.query: Treasury proposed regulations prohibited foreign entity effective control material assistance safe harbor tables notice

items.question: Were PFE proposed regulations or safe-harbor tables published after May 2026?
items.result_summary: The results were off-topic: section 892 regulations, OFAC, a DOE FEOC page and OMB. Nothing on PFE proposed regulations or tables appeared.
items.interpretation: Newer PFE guidance could not be confirmed either way, so it is marked unverified.

params.query: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material anode plant Morowali IMIP Kendal capacity

items.question: Where is BTR's Indonesian anode plant, and what is its capacity and status?
items.result_summary: A BTR press release (Aug 2024) and Petromindo say PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material operates at IMIP (Morowali, Central Sulawesi) and the Kendal Industrial Park (Central Java). Phase 1 is 80,000 tpa ($478M), and Phase 2 adds 80,000 tpa ($299M) for 160,000 tpa, expected in late 2025.
items.interpretation: This is BTR's main non-China anode source and a plausible third-country route for Chinese-owned anode capacity. Battery-Tech Network reports a 70/30 BTR/Stellar Investment ownership split, which is not primary-verified.

params.query: BTR New Material Morocco anode material plant Tangier investment

items.question: What is BTR's Morocco anode plant, and where is it?
items.result_summary: In Aug 2024 BTR announced a 60,000 tpa integrated anode project in Tangier Tech City through BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology, with investment of no more than $366M and about two years of construction. A separate 50,000 tpa cathode project is also in Tangier.
items.interpretation: Morocco has a US free-trade agreement, which may explain the siting. Its current operating status in 2026 is not confirmed.

params.query: Zhongke Electric Oman lithium battery anode material project Sohar

items.question: What is Zhongke Electric's Oman anode project?
items.result_summary: Gulf News and ChemAnalyst report a Sohar Freezone anode plant of up to 200,000 tpa in three phases, at roughly $1-1.1bn. GraphiteHub says it broke ground on 8 May 2026, targets 2027 production and that Zhongke cancelled planned anode projects including one in Morocco in June 2026.
items.interpretation: Oman is an emerging third-country anode hub for a respondent group in the AD case (Zhongke Shinzoom). The groundbreaking date and the Morocco cancellation come from a single trade site.

params.query: Chinese battery anode graphite producer operating plants in Indonesia; detect rerouting through third-country plants into US supply chains

items.question: What does Sayari's own tradecraft say about tracing a supply chain like this?
items.result_summary: Five guidance entries came back: supply-chain pitfalls and data gaps, free-zone opacity red flags, a trade-based investigation workflow, a tool-selection guide and a bearer-share protocol.
items.interpretation: Three rules shaped the method: resolve the entity before anything else, keep freight forwarders out of supplier lists, and treat missing trade data as a gap, not a negative.

params.query: Same company appears as several fragmented records with different addresses (Morowali IMIP, Kendal, Jakarta Barat) in Indonesia

items.question: Is there Indonesia-specific guidance on merging fragmented company records?
items.result_summary: No entries. The country filter plus entity-resolution type returned 0 results.
items.interpretation: The guidance library is thin for Indonesia. We dropped the country filter and asked again (s004).

items.question: What exactly do the risk flags on the seed records mean?
items.purpose: Read flag definitions before using them (INV-6)
items.result_summary: Definitions for six flags. '_adjacent' means one hop from a flagged entity through any relationship. 'psa_' means the path runs through a 'Possibly the Same As' link. 'forced_labor_uflpa_origin_subtier' means a UFLPA-listed entity appears in tier 2 or 3 of the supplier network in the last 730 days.
items.interpretation: None of these flags says the plant itself is listed. They describe neighbours. We show them as context, never as findings about the company.

params.query: fragmented entity records same company multiple records how to decide same legal entity

items.question: How should we decide whether several sparse records are one legal entity?
items.result_summary: Returned Sayari's 'Entity Resolution Quality Reasoning' entry: anchor on identifiers, registry IDs and structured addresses; same group or similar name is not enough; merge only when evidence supports one legal entity.
items.interpretation: Became our merge rule: a matching street address plus matching name stem gives an Inferred 'possibly same as' link; a name match alone stays a Lead.

items.question: Who is the main Indonesian record, and what identifies it?
items.result_summary: PT. Indonesia BTR New Energy Material. Addresses in both IMIP Morowali (Central Sulawesi) and Kendal Industrial Estate (Central Java). Indonesian tax ID, LEI 254900G3L2Z0HNRV7W43. Sources: UK, Japan, South Korea and China trade data plus the LEI registry. 78 shipments sent, 4,083 received. Flags include chinese_soe_adjacent and several forced-labor sub-tier and PSA flags.
items.interpretation: This is the anchor record: the only one with registry-grade identifiers. It receives far more than it sends, which fits a processing plant that imports raw material.

items.question: Is the Kendal-only record the same company?
items.result_summary: 'PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Materi' (name cut off). Address: Jl. Indraprasta No. 8, Kendal Industrial Estate. Only source: USA Imports (2021 to present). 37 shipments sent, none received. No identifiers.
items.interpretation: Same street address as the anchor and a truncated version of its name. It exists only because US customs records spelled the shipper differently. That makes it the US-facing view of the same plant.

items.question: Is the Jakarta Barat record the same company?
items.result_summary: Exact legal name, but the only address is 'Jakarta Barat'. Only source: Indonesia Berita Negara company gazette. No trade, no identifiers.
items.interpretation: Probably the registry filing for the same PT (Jakarta is a common registered-office location), but nothing ties it to the plant except the name. Kept as a Lead.

items.question: Who does the plant trade with, and does Sayari hold any ownership links for it?
items.result_summary: No shareholder or parent relationships at all. Trade relationships only: ships_to 23, receives_from 90. Named ships_to partners include Ultium Cells Warren (USA), Ultium Cells Spring Hill (USA), Samsung SDI, Aminco Resources LLC, BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd., FBKorea and Ferrolux GmbH.
items.interpretation: The first sign of a US trail: two Ultium Cells plants appear as buyers. The parent's name appears only as a trade partner, not as an owner.

items.question: Who owns the Indonesian plant?
items.result_summary: 0 results.
items.interpretation: Sayari holds no shareholder data for this PT. Ownership has to come from open sources and is labelled that way. This is the central blind spot of the case.

items.question: What has the plant shipped to the US?
items.result_summary: Returned 10,000 unrelated US-bound shipments (photo paper, auto parts, Brazilian flake graphite). The shipper_name filter was not applied.
items.interpretation: Same failure seen in our earlier project: name filters can silently drop. Every result has to be re-checked against the supplier field before it counts.

items.question: Who did the US-import record ship to?
items.result_summary: ships_to: Tesla Inc, Ultium Cells Warren, General Motors. Source: USA Imports only.
items.interpretation: US customs data links this record to three US buyers, one of them shared with the anchor record (Ultium Cells Warren). Shared buyers are extra evidence that the two records are one plant.

items.question: Can we see the Indonesia → Ultium shipments directly?
items.result_summary: The receiver filter was ignored: results were palm oil to ADM, electronics and similar. One relevant row: 'carbon anode materials, HS 3801.90' from Indonesia to a Tesla warehouse in Santa Clara (Aug 2026), with no supplier named.
items.interpretation: Partial. It shows anode material does leave Indonesia for the US, but an unnamed shipper can't be tied to the plant.

items.question: Who supplies the plant?
items.result_summary: 90 suppliers: 65 in China, then Mozambique (4), Madagascar (3), Hong Kong (3), USA (5) and others. They include BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd., BTR New Material Group Sales Co., Ltd., and Shenzhen Ruiqing New Energy Technology, whose registered address is 'Room 1108, BTR Building, No. 8 Guangyuan 4th Road, Guangming District, Shenzhen'.
items.interpretation: Most of the plant's inputs come from China, including from the parent group and a trader registered in the parent group's own building.

items.question: Does the plant import the same product (graphite) that it exports?
items.result_summary: HS 3801 (artificial graphite) China → Indonesia from BTR New Material Group (Dec 2025) and Shenzhen Ruiqing (Dec 2023 to Jun 2026). HS 2504 (natural graphite) from Mozambique (Twigg Exploration & Mining), Madagascar (ERG Madagascar, others), the UAE (Syrah Global DMCC) and China. HS 2713 (petroleum coke, an anode precursor) from China, Japan, Germany and Switzerland.
items.interpretation: Yes. Artificial graphite comes in from China and artificial graphite goes out to the US. But the plant also buys non-Chinese natural graphite and coke, so trade data alone can't say which input ended up in which export.

items.question: Using HS code filters only, how many Indonesian suppliers send anode material to the US?
items.interpretation: A query that looks correct returns nothing. The free-text word 'anode' doesn't match records described as 'artificial graphite'. This is how a trail goes dark.

items.question: Same question as a supplier rollup.
items.interpretation: Confirms the feasibility-probe result. Rollups are blind here; the shipment search by name (s017) is what works.

items.question: Put the plant's name in the free-text query instead of the filter. What reached the US?
items.result_summary: 19 shipment rows, all from BTR Indonesia records. HS 3801.10 artificial graphite to Ultium Cells Warren (Jun–Aug 2025, 3 rows), Ultium Cells Spring Hill (Aug 2025, 2), SK Battery America (Aug 2025, 1), StarPlus Energy (Mar–Apr 2025, 3), General Motors (Aug 2025, 1; plus HS 3801.90 in Dec 2024, 1), Tesla (Aug 2025, 1), Aminco Resources (Sep 2025, 3) and Larpen Metallurgical Service (Jun 2026, 2). Two rows to StarPlus carry a cosmetics HS code.
items.interpretation: The key transactional evidence: dated, HS-coded shipments from the Indonesian plant to five US battery or auto makers. Two of the shippers are separate Sayari records (fragments 4 and 5).

items.question: Confirm the US-import record's buyers in the graph.
items.result_summary: Three ships_to links: Ultium Cells Warren (Warren, Ohio), General Motors and Tesla Inc.
items.interpretation: Matches s011. The same three US buyers appear whether you start from the US-import record or from the shipment search.

items.question: What is the shortest link between the Indonesian plant and BTR in China?
items.result_summary: One hop: a ships_to trade link. No ownership path.
items.interpretation: In Sayari, the plant and its reported parent are connected by trade, not by any registry record.

items.question: Which Indonesian or Moroccan companies does BTR own, according to registry data?
items.result_summary: One path: BTR → Changzhou Liyuan New Energy Technology (China) → Liyuan (Indonesia) New Energy Co. Both links are shareholder_of. The anode plant is not in the list.
items.interpretation: Sayari can see BTR's registry links in general, so the missing link to the anode plant is a coverage gap for this PT, not a tool failure.

items.question: Is the plant connected to sanctioned or watch-listed parties?
items.result_summary: No direct hit. Ten sanctioned parties two hops away, every path through a logistics firm or trader (e.g. Sinotrans Central China, Sky Fortune Freight, Mitsubishi Corporation) to an unrelated Russian, Sudanese or Turkish company.
items.interpretation: Noise from shared freight forwarders, exactly what the guidance warned about. Not a finding about the plant.

items.question: Who is the 'PT Indonesia BTR New Energy' shipper that sent graphite to GM?
items.result_summary: A fourth record. Its address field starts with 'MATERIAL. Jl. Indraprasta No. 8 Kwsn Ind Kendal', meaning the end of the company name spilled into the address. Sources: China, Indonesia, Malaysia and US trade data.
items.interpretation: Same street address and the missing word of the name. Possibly the same as the anchor (Inferred).

items.question: Who is the 'PT Indonesia BTR' shipper that sent graphite to Tesla and GM?
items.result_summary: A fifth record. Same Kendal address (Jl. Indraprasta No. 8). Sources: Indonesia, Japan and South Korea trade data. 12 shipments sent.
items.interpretation: Same street address, shortened name. Possibly the same as the anchor (Inferred). Five Sayari records describe what is most likely one plant.

items.question: Where does US-bound artificial graphite come from?
items.result_summary: About 47,000 HS 3801.10 shipments to the US since Jan 2024. Top departure countries: Spain 8,862, China 5,244, India 3,661, Germany 3,535, Morocco 3,088, Netherlands 2,993, Mexico 2,939, Belgium 2,385. General Motors is among the top ten buyers.
items.interpretation: Indonesia is a small corridor by count, so the BTR trail would be easy to miss in aggregate data. Morocco, where BTR is building a second plant, is already a large corridor and is the natural Case 2.

params.query: IEA China share of global battery anode material production graphite percent

items.question: How much of the world's battery anode material comes from China?
items.result_summary: Electrive's summary of the IEA's 2025 battery report: China supplies over 90% of anode materials, mostly graphite, and does about 80% of graphite mining and over 90% of refining. It also notes that Indonesia is expected to add some diversification.
items.interpretation: This is why third-country anode plants matter: almost all battery-grade graphite processing is in China, so any 'non-Chinese' anode supply is worth checking.

params.query: graphite share of lithium-ion battery anode by weight EV battery graphite kg per vehicle

items.question: How much of an EV battery is graphite?
items.result_summary: A USITC working paper on graphite in EV batteries (Table C.2, citing Argonne's GREET model) gives graphite as 21% of cell weight for NMC-622 cells, 22.1% for NCA and 16.8% for LFP.
items.interpretation: Graphite is roughly a fifth of a battery cell by weight, more than any other mineral, so its origin matters for tax-credit rules.

items.question: Does Sayari hold any Zhongke entity in Oman?
items.result_summary: 0 results.
items.interpretation: No Oman entity under the group name. This is the first sign the plant isn't in the data yet.

items.question: Which record is the listed parent?
items.result_summary: 513 results came back (the limit was ignored) and the output was saved to a file. Among them were 湖南中科电气股份有限公司 (-jDI6N9q1MWnPT0ujf-8iw), an English-name duplicate 'HUNAN ZHONGKE ELECTRIC CO., LTD.' (Mn2FeoIt2w0McDIDjkIrxg), and Changsha, Chifeng and sales-department branches. Most hits are unrelated companies called Zhongke.
items.interpretation: We picked the Chinese-name record because it carries a USCC and the listed-security links. The name is very common, so we parsed the results; we didn't read them by eye.

items.question: Can one query find both romanisations?
items.result_summary: 0 results.
items.interpretation: The OR query with quoted phrases returned nothing, though each name exists (see s305). The query syntax didn't work as documented.

items.question: Which Sayari records are POSCO Future M?
items.purpose: Resolve the company and its fragments
items.result_summary: 19 records. The main one (株式会社POSCO CHEMICAL, DART CIK 00155276) carries both the old and new names and addresses in Pohang, Gwangyang and Sejong. At least ten more records use the POSCO Future M or POSCO Chemical name, several with the same Pohang (110 Sinhang-ro) or Gwangyang (45 Yulchonsandan 8-ro) street addresses. Two records name the freight forwarder LX Pantos acting for POSCO Future M; one is the Canadian subsidiary in Bécancour.
items.interpretation: Unlike Case 1, the main record has a registry identifier (Korea's DART disclosure ID), so the anchor is solid. Same-address fragments are treated as 'possibly the same as'.

items.question: Who ships artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) from Morocco to the US?
items.result_summary: 646 suppliers, but only country buckets came back (India 261, USA 203, China 194, Spain 186...). No supplier names. Buyer countries include Colombia, Mexico, Ecuador and Guatemala, which is odd for a US-arrival filter.
items.interpretation: The supplier-scope facet can't name shippers. Non-US buyer countries were a first hint that the bucket is not what it seems.

items.question: What records does Sayari hold for BTR's Moroccan subsidiary?
items.result_summary: 6 records: two registry companies in Morocco (BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology, RC 142409 with an LEI; BTR Mediterranean Anode New Material Technology, RC 149725) and four customs-data fragments with no country.
items.interpretation: Two separate legal entities plus four trade fragments. One fragment shares the registry address (Lot 25, Tanger Tech).

items.question: Who owns POSCO Future M, and who does it trade with?
items.purpose: Ownership and trade partners of the main record
items.result_summary: Registered 1971-05-13. Business purpose includes refractories and secondary-battery manufacturing. Shareholder: 포스코홀딩스(주) (POSCO Holdings) with 58.2%, from Korea's DART disclosure database. Owns the Canadian subsidiary. Trade counts: 10,199 sent, 1,788 received. Ships to Tesla, VinFast and a Polish logistics agent; receives from Huayou New Energy (Quzhou) and a Shanghai supply-chain firm.
items.interpretation: Ownership is a registry record with a percentage. The parent is Korean. This is the opposite of Case 1, where Sayari had no owner for BTR's plant.

items.question: Who owns and runs BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology?
items.result_summary: SASU registered 2023-10-09. 100% shareholder and beneficial owner: BNUO International Holding Pte. Ltd (Singapore). Its general manager is the same executive who appears at the Singapore and Jiangsu companies. Trade count 0 sent, 0 received.
items.interpretation: Unlike Case 1, the registry data names a shareholder. The registry record itself has no trade.

items.question: Who owns BTR Mediterranean Anode New Material Technology?
items.result_summary: Registered 2024-05-03 in Tangier. 100% shareholder: Rian International Holding Pte. Ltd (Singapore). Director Zerui Fang. No trade.
items.interpretation: A second BTR company in Tangier, held through a different Singapore holding company.

items.question: How many suppliers ship artificial graphite (HS 3801.10) from Vietnam to the US since 2024?
items.result_summary: 5 suppliers. Facets do not name them; supplier-country buckets include KOR, CHN and others because they list every country a supplier is linked to.
items.interpretation: A thin corridor. Five names is few enough to check one by one.

items.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Malaysia to the US since 2024?
items.result_summary: 2 suppliers.
items.interpretation: The thinnest corridor of the five.

items.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Thailand to the US since 2024?
items.result_summary: 8 suppliers.
items.interpretation: Thin; worth listing every name.

items.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Mexico to the US since 2024?
items.result_summary: 347 suppliers; buyer-country buckets led by USA (555). Many supplier risk flags are 'psa_' or sub-tier flags.
items.interpretation: By far the biggest corridor, but size alone says nothing about battery content.

items.question: How many suppliers ship HS 3801.10 from Korea to the US since 2024?
items.result_summary: 107 suppliers.
items.interpretation: Second-largest corridor; Korea has its own anode industry.

items.question: Does the ownership chain reach BTR in China?
items.result_summary: 2 owners: BNUO International Holding (1 hop) and BTR New Material Group (jeHf5QJt0JXowTiCA8JiIQ) at path length 4, via a 'possibly same as' Singapore registry record of BNUO.
items.interpretation: Yes. BTR New Material Group is visible as the ultimate owner, with one 'possibly same as' step.

items.question: Does the second company's chain reach BTR?
items.result_summary: 2 owners: Rian International Holding (1 hop) and a Singapore record of 'BTR New Material Group Co., Ltd.' (UEN T23UF7645F) at path length 3, via a 'possibly same as' Rian record.
items.interpretation: This chain also ends at BTR, but at a Singapore filing record that Sayari has not merged with the main BTR entity.

items.question: Is there any Chinese owner anywhere up the chain?
items.result_summary: 50 owner paths returned, all one hop and all Korean: POSCO Holdings (three records under Korean and English names), POSCO (주)포스코, the National Pension Service (국민연금공단), Pohang University of Science and Technology, and about 40 named Korean individuals (DART shareholding filings by officers).
items.interpretation: No Chinese owner appears at any level. The individual names are officers who report small holdings; they are not controlling owners.

items.question: What exactly links the Moroccan plant to BTR?
items.result_summary: Path: BTR Mediterranean ← BNUO (Moroccan record) ~ BNUO Pte. Ltd. (Singapore registry, possibly same as) ← BTR (Jiangsu) New Material Technology ← BTR New Material Group.
items.interpretation: An ownership path, not a trade link. Compare Case 1, where the shortest path was a shipment.

items.question: Who is behind BNUO International Holding in Singapore?
items.result_summary: UEN 202332562W, registered 2023-08-14, holding company at Duo Tower, Fraser Street. 100% shareholder BTR (Jiangsu). Its CEO is also general manager of the Moroccan company (an individual, named in Sayari). Also owns Envolvic International Holding. Mass-address and nominee-director flags.
items.interpretation: The Singapore step is a corporate-services shell, but its shareholder is a BTR subsidiary. The same executive also runs the Moroccan company, which supports the 'possibly same as' link.

items.question: Who are the five Vietnam suppliers?
items.result_summary: Minh Thinh Loi (Da Nang, 30 shipments, latest 24 Jan 2025), HS Hyosung Global Logistics Vina (2), Hyosung TNC (1), Graphite India (1), Samsung Electronics Vietnam Thai Nguyen (1, 2019).
items.interpretation: No Chinese-owned anode maker. One local parts maker, Korean groups and a logistics firm.

items.question: Who are the eight Thailand suppliers?
items.result_summary: Shanghai Supreme International Freight Forwarding, T.C. Pharmaceutical (three records), ECU Worldwide (Thailand), AC Container Line, China Highwin (Thailand), Topasia International Logistics.
items.interpretation: Forwarders and a drinks maker. China Highwin is the only Chinese-named one; checked further.

items.question: Who are the two Malaysia suppliers?
items.result_summary: Graphite India Limited (1 shipment) and PAC Worldwide Corp (1, Apr 2025).
items.interpretation: No Malaysian producer ships HS 3801.10 to the US in this data.

items.question: Where do POSCO Future M's graphite and carbon inputs come from?
items.result_summary: 18 supplier rows. Natural graphite (HS 2504) from China: Zhanjiang Juxin New Energy (two records, Jul–Dec 2023), Qingdao Haida New Energy Materials (Jun–Sep 2023), Qingdao Zhongshuo New Energy (Aug 2023), Qingdao Kuntuo New Material (Jul–Sep 2023). Artificial graphite (HS 3801) from China: Qingdao Kuntuo (Sep 2023) and Qingdao Qingbei Carbon Products (Oct 2021 – Jul 2022). Natural graphite from Twigg Exploration & Mining, Mozambique (Jun 2022). Petroleum coke (HS 2713) from China EPT (Jul 2022) and P66 Ltd, UK (Mar 2022). Coal-tar pitch and oils from Rain Carbon Germany via Belgium and the Netherlands (Nov 2021 – Jan 2024). Carbon black (HS 2803) from several of the Qingdao and Zhanjiang suppliers.
items.interpretation: Chinese natural graphite does flow into this Korean-owned producer. Every Chinese graphite row is dated 2023 or earlier.

items.question: Is BTR (Jiangsu) wholly owned by BTR?
items.result_summary: BTR (Jiangsu) New Material Technology, Changzhou, USCC 91320413MA1NAU5H7M, registered 2017-01-16. 100% shareholder BTR New Material Group. Holds 100% of BNUO. Its chairman is the same executive.
items.interpretation: Every step is 100%. The same executive's name appears at the Jiangsu, Singapore and Moroccan companies (a cross-script name match).

items.question: What has the Moroccan plant shipped or received?
items.result_summary: 10 rows, all inbound from China to Morocco, Nov 2025 – Jun 2026: racks and pipelines (Master Union Logistics, 3), steel pipes (Shenzhen Haizhuolian Energy, 4), machinery and unspecified goods (Sinotrans, 2), one row from China Construction Yangtze International Engineering. items.question: Does POSCO Future M say it uses Chinese spherical graphite?
items.result_summary: KED Global: Korea relies entirely on Chinese imports for natural and spherical graphite; POSCO Future M plans to make spherical graphite at home. Korea Herald: the Sejong plant 'currently reprocesses spherical graphite … imported from China' and aims to phase out Chinese intermediates by 2027; a new Saemangeum plant (subsidiary Future Graph) will use African graphite. POSCO E&C: Sejong makes natural-graphite anode. POSCO newsroom: same Africa → Saemangeum → Sejong plan.
items.interpretation: The company itself confirms the Chinese spherical-graphite dependence that Sayari shows up to Dec 2023, and says it continues. So the Sayari stop after 2023 is a coverage gap.

items.question: Which US customers has POSCO Future M announced, and what does the Pohang plant use?
items.result_summary: POSCO Future M newsroom: a binding six-year, KRW 939.3 billion deal to supply Ultium Cells (GM–LG Energy Solution) with artificial graphite anode from the Pohang plant; an earlier deal to supply Sejong anode to Ultium. Pohang artificial graphite uses needle coke from PMC Tech, a group carbon subsidiary. Businesskorea repeats the Ultium deal. Korea Herald (t401) says the Pohang synthetic graphite uses coke by-products from POSCO steelmaking. One aggregator site (energy-solutions.co) gives unsourced percentages; we did not use it.
items.interpretation: Two product lines with different input risks: natural-graphite anode (Sejong) relies on Chinese spherical graphite; artificial-graphite anode (Pohang) is presented as Korean feedstock. Sayari rows can't say which plant made a given shipment.

items.question: Is Zichen Malaysia the company building the plant?
items.purpose: Cross-check the registry entity with the company's announcement
items.result_summary: SMM and Mysteel report that the project is 'undertaken by Zichen Malaysia Sdn. Bhd.'; a post quoting the announcement calls it Putailai's 'wholly-owned overseas subsidiary'.
